headline: Share of one-person households ranks lowest citywide, while park space ranks last here.
summary:
Garfield Ridge, West Lawn, West Elsdon, and Archer Heights fall inside Ward 23, on Chicago's Southwest Side. It comes in 32nd citywide, with a score of 39.76, below the midpoint of the fifty but well clear of the bottom. Its strongest measures point to a tightly knit residential area. Share of one-person households ranks lowest in Chicago here, meaning shared and family households are more common than in any other ward. Licensed tobacco retailers per resident rank 2nd, so only one ward has fewer of them for the people it holds, and landlord profit on rental units ranks 3rd on two separate measures, meaning renters here keep more of what they pay than in most of the city.

Where the ward falls short is public and gathering space. It ranks last in Chicago for parks, with just 4 mapped inside its boundaries, for civic and cultural places (18 of them), and for houses of worship per resident. It also ranks last for cars per household, with the highest average number of vehicles per home in the city, and last for the modeled share of adults expected to visit a bar weekly. Put together, the picture is a residential, car-dependent stretch of the Southwest Side with little built infrastructure for public life outside the home.
reading_the_rankings: A few of these numbers are softer than they look. That last-place finish comes with an asterisk. Thirty-six wards cluster together on the measure labeled review count, value 1,070, none more than two points apart, which turns the whole stretch into an effective tie rather than a real last place. Between the thirteenth-best ward and the thirty-eighth on that same measure there are only two points, so most of the fifty land close to the middle no matter where the number falls. Two of the strengths are modeled estimates rather than counts of anything that happened here. The 3rd-place rank for adults with no religious affiliation, 19.4 percent, and the last-place rank for adults expected to visit a bar weekly, 4.1 percent, both come from survey-based statistical models. Wards with similar demographics tend to produce close to the same modeled number by construction, and this one is flagged low confidence by whoever built it. Read both as a general pattern built from the area's makeup, not a figure gathered from Ward 23 residents directly.

news.headline: 'Moving Archer Forward' Initiative Aims To Bring 800 New Housing Units To Archer Avenue
news.note: City and regional transit planners unveiled a long-range plan to redevelop the Archer Avenue corridor from Bridgeport to Garfield Ridge, with new housing, retail space and street upgrades.

news.headline: Garfield Ridge Satellite Center Celebrates 30 Years Serving Seniors
news.note: The Garfield Ridge Satellite Center marked 30 years of serving seniors with a City Council resolution and a month of activities for older residents.
